votes.reasoning: This is a re-vote on the reworked tracker. Each crossing records previous = the mark it replaced (line 347). When it fails, unmark sets highestNotified back to that previous value instead of dropping the key (line 288). Trace: 70 is delivered and its pending entry removed; 90 fails, so highest is 70 again. The next 75 reading does not re-send 70, and the next 95 reading re-sends 90. The 'restores the delivered lower mark', 'still retried' and 'unmark restores' tests pass. Reversal to HEAD turned the rollback test RED (count 3 == 2) and the tracker unit test RED; restored byte-identical.

Round 2 rework: unmark now restores the value in pending[key][threshold].previous (NotificationService.swift:288) and no longer calls removeValue on the key. The guard-let on the pending entry replaces the old 'still the recorded mark' check, and the doc (:276-283) explains both the old reason and the new one. rearmParked (:317) reuses unmark instead of copying the restore rule. The Crossing typealias is kept. The test names say what they assert, for example failed_higher_crossing_keeps_delivered_lower_mark. Assertions compare Int, [String] and String? values, so none are the vacuous Bool forms.

The r2 rework (the mark it replaced now lives in tracker.pending instead of being passed through send/deliveryFinished) removes the previousMark parameter the r1 diff had added. The surface shrinks back to the pre-r1 signatures. Only NotificationService.swift and the two notification test files are touched for this id.
